chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad informed me, from his father, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Simāʿah, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
If you have performed part of your wudu (ablution), then a need arises for you such that your wudu dries up, then repeat your wudu, for wudu is not to be divided.

key_terms.حَاجَةٌ: a need or interruption that arises during the act
key_terms.لَا يُبَعَّضُ: it is not divided, meaning it is not to be performed in separated disconnected parts
key_terms.وُضُوئِكَ: your wudu (ablution), meaning the ritual washing being performed
key_terms.يَبِسَ: it dried, referring to the moisture of the prior wudu acts

ai.seo_question: If my wudu dries before I finish it, do I have to repeat the whole wudu?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about continuity in wudu (ablution). If a person interrupts the act and the moisture of the previous washing dries, the wudu must be restarted, because wudu is not performed in separated parts.
